title: France, between rain and light
subtitle: A railway arrival in Metz and a long day across Paris, from the Louvre and riverside palaces to the Eiffel Tower and the rain-lit streets of Montmartre.
category: From Lorraine to the streets of Paris

cover.alt: Visitors crossing the courtyard before the Louvre’s glass pyramid beneath a bright, cloud-filled sky.
cover.caption: Visitors crossing the courtyard before the Louvre’s glass pyramid beneath a bright, cloud-filled sky.

chapters.title: Across Lorraine to Metz
paragraphs: Fields pass the train window before the stone towers and broad station square of Metz. The photographs pause among the surrounding streets and beneath the station’s vaulted ceiling.

chapters.title: From the Louvre to the gardens
chapters.location: Louvre · Tuileries · Place de la Concorde, Paris
paragraphs: The day begins among the Louvre’s stone façades and covered arches. Green chairs, quiet paths, new leaves and carved figures continue the walk through the Tuileries towards the fountains of Concorde.

chapters.title: Palace façades and museum rooms
chapters.location: Petit Palais · Grand Palais · Seine, Paris
paragraphs: Small garden details lead to monumental façades. Inside the Petit Palais, paintings and a sweeping staircase give way to the river and the gilded figures above Pont Alexandre III.

chapters.title: A pause and the courtyards of Invalides
paragraphs: A narrow passage and a café breakfast mark a pause between walks. The route then enters the broad stone courtyards of Les Invalides and continues towards its gilded dome.

chapters.title: Shops and flowers around Rue Cler
paragraphs: The next streets are lined with cafés, fruit stalls, books and flowers. A slower walk takes in the shopfronts and the people moving between them.

chapters.title: Above and below the Eiffel Tower
paragraphs: At ground level, artists and visitors gather beneath the ironwork. Higher up, the gardens, river and dense city blocks spread out in different directions before the view turns back into the tower’s steel frame.

chapters.title: Stonework around the Arc and Chaillot
paragraphs: The Arc de Triomphe fills the next views: carved reliefs, the deep vault and flowers at the tomb below. The walk continues past a museum façade and a planted square in Chaillot.

chapters.title: Rain and evening light in Montmartre
paragraphs: Sloping streets lead towards Sacré-Cœur, its mosaics and stained glass. Outside, painted walls, small shops and a carousel accompany the descent; the evening ends among reflections on the wet streets.
